title: bimodal-sequence-mixer-with-quantile-histogram-reporter
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: We need representative traffic generators that capture multi-modal sequence length behavior observed in production (short queries bursty with occasional long-form requests). Motivation: Current workload runners bias toward single-mode (short or long) sequences which underestimates batch formation and KV-cache reuse patterns. Summary: Introduce a bimodal sequence mixer that stochastically composes workload traces from two configurable sequence-length distributions and a complementary quantile-histogram reporter to capture per-kernel latency shift across token quantiles. This PR adds: 1) a lightweight generator that merges a short-tail Poisson sampler with a long-tail Pareto sampler, 2) an executor harness that maintains KV priming per session and emits per-request tokenized metadata, 3) a quantile-histogram reporter pipeline that buckets per-token and per-request latencies and exports histograms in the bench CSV and Prometheus-compatible textfile, 4) small runtime instrumentation hooks for kernel-tagging and primer-hit flags, and 5) a reproducible seed/trace recorder for replay. Checklist: - [x] Implement generator and executor harness - [x] Add reporter and exporters - [x] Add unit tests for sampler distributions - [x] Add integration test comparing a single-mode baseline to bimodal run - [x] Update bench lab README with usage and CSV schema - [x] Validate Prometheus export format and examples Usage notes: the harness supports --short-rate, --long-alpha, --mix-ratio, and --primer-size flags. Test plan: ran bench-suite CI with synthetic mix and a small GPU-backed local runner. Compared p50/p90/p99 token latency histograms against single-mode baseline and observed expected uplift in tail coverage. Also ran exporter locally and verified Prometheus textfile ingestion in dev cluster. Related: ENG-1284 (tail coverage improvement), ENG-1309 (KV priming fidelity).
